description: The wire error codes of the admin HTTP surface (/admin/v1), each with its one HTTP status and when it applies. Every error body is {"error":"<code>"}, application/json, and nothing else: no description, no value of the request or of a row (no ID, name, constraint, member or claim name), no key byte, no version member (ERR-072). A fixture refers to a code as _wire/errors.v1.json#<code>. Source of the mapping: the module docs of service/src/admin_http/mod.rs, "Errors" and "Wire codes" (the S4 PR, lead decision 2026-11-24 and the ruling of 2026-11-26). Entries marked origin "reused" are the frozen reasons of errors-retry section 2 (ERR-070) or OAuth error values (RFC 6749); entries marked "proposed" are named by no other catalogue and are inferred. The wire codes of the token endpoint are not in this file. tests/harness/wire_errors.rs pins every code, status and Retry-After here to service::admin_http::ErrorCode.

applies_when: the request has no verified peer identity (no client certificate the acceptor verified)
a verified identity names no usable credential: none that is enabled and unrevoked, of an enabled operator
an unknown path or method under the router, when the request has no peer
unauthenticated.notes: The two causes give the same bytes (ERR-001, ERR-010, ERR-011). It is not an oracle: the peer proved possession of the key in the handshake and learns the state of its own credential only.

applies_when: a usable credential has no binding of the role and scope the request needs: one value for every cause (another role, another scope, a disabled binding or operator)
a principal kind the path does not reach (PrincipalKindNotAllowed; IR-043)
an approval by the requester itself (SelfApproval) or by a credential without the role
forbidden.notes: Decided before any target is read: a refused caller learns nothing of the target, not even whether it exists.

applies_when: the target object does not exist, or exists outside the caller's scope: the same bytes for both
an unknown path or method under the router (HEAD included), when the request has a peer
not_found.notes: Never says whether another tenant's object exists.

applies_when: a malformed path, query or cursor: another query parameter, a repeated one, a limit that is not an unsigned 32-bit integer, a cursor with a NUL character

a submitted value that breaks a syntax or value rule, whatever the stored state: a column check or not-null violation, a reserved actor ID, a missing required predicate, a malformed public key identity, a keyset upload the upload checks refuse, a private member in provenance, the destination of an egress create or a trust source write that fails the destination rule
invalid_request.notes: A value the request did not submit (a stored plan's or a stored row's) is the stored state's: 409, not 400. The status depends on the request's bytes only, so it is no oracle about the store.

applies_when: the expected revision of an update, disable or approval no longer matches the stored one: read the target again
a duplicate (AlreadyExists) or a guard refusal
a missing or disabled referenced row, an assignment that is not active, an egress entry that is still enabled
a keyset version window that overlaps another's or too many enabled versions
a trust source destination with no enabled egress entry
an egress enable whose stored destination fails the destination rule (InvalidStoredDestination)
an approval whose echo does not match or whose requester is no longer authorized
a gated write where the second-approver flow has no operation kind for it yet
the operation is consumed, revoked, expired or not of the flow
the stored plan fails a check at approval: a keyset upload, a private member in provenance, a source destination, or a column constraint, which run at approve only (D7)
the write's tenant is disabled and the write is not disable-only (a tenant enable is allowed)
a well-formed write that widens, without the acknowledge_widening the server's rule asks for (a gated trust, keyset, source or egress write, or an approval)
widening_not_acknowledged.notes: 422 only for this case (the second-approver proposal, section 10).

applies_when: the ID generator has no ID to give (SourceFailed, Exhausted): nothing is written

a server or data-integrity error: an unreadable stored timestamp, a stored plan that fails its integrity check, a stored keyset version or fingerprint that does not decode or match, a tripwire (same-tenant operation, distinct approver), an unsupported isolation level
any store failure not otherwise mapped: a decode failure, an unknown SQLSTATE, a constraint not in the known list
the store or another dependency is unavailable: an I/O or TLS failure, pool timeout or closure, SQLSTATE class 08 or 53, 57P01 to 57P05, the validation worker unavailable (no Retry-After)

a retryable failure: a serialization failure or deadlock (40001, 40P01), a lock or statement timeout (55P03, 57014), a busy validation worker, no instance security policy row (effectively unreachable after authorization): with Retry-After: 1
auth_unavailable.notes: Retry-After: 1 is present when a retry of the whole request may succeed (the second-approver proposal's mapping).
